blocking_findings.summary: [P1] Remove the remaining “legacy” naming from the live repository tests (apps/core/test/integration/permission-decision-memory.postgres.integration.test.ts:33): The test still calls `put`, `get`, `list`, and `revoke` “legacy” APIs and repeats that label in its fixture names.

ASKFLOOR-1-T3a-AC2: PORT + REPOSITORY. `PermissionDecisionMemoryKind` gains `'human_decision'`; the row and put types gain optional `outcome?: HumanDecisionOutcome` (`allow | deny`), `scope?: HumanDecisionScope` (`exact | kind | place`), `scopeKey?`, `actingPersonId?`, `actingPersonLabel?` (closed typed enums exported from the port; no string literals elsewhere). The existing methods `put`, `get`, `list` and `revoke` serve the four NON-HUMAN kinds (classifier verdicts, remembered denies, trusted roots, standing grants — live code, not compatibility code; nothing in the diff may be named or commented "legacy"): each REFUSES `kind: 'human_decision'` (throws `HumanDecisionRequiresTypedAccessError`, a named domain error in the port, raised by one guard `assertNonHumanKind` — the human path has its own person-scoped methods below), `put` keeps today's conflict target, and an unfiltered `list` (no `kind`) EXCLUDES human rows (`kind <> 'human_decision'`), so no non-human path can read or revoke across persons (0154/0118). NEW `putHumanDecision(input) → Promise<{ id: string; status: 'inserted' | 'refreshed' }>`: requires all four human fields and a v4-UUID-shaped `id` (a missing field or a malformed id throws before any SQL — the same guard style as `assertPersistable`, `:17-34`), always `lookupIdentity = scopeKey`, `decision = outcome`, `principal = canonicalTool`; it runs in ONE transaction: select the ACTIVE row for `(app_id, agent_folder, acting_person_id, scope, scope_key)` (the human partial index's key) — if one exists it is REFRESHED in place with `outcome`, `decision`, `reason`, `acting_person_label`, `effect_hash`, `rail_version`, `effect_schema_version`, `created_at` AND `provenance` re-encoded (AC5) with the STORED id, and the STORED id is returned with `status: 'refreshed'` (the caller's fresh id is discarded — an opposite-outcome write for the same authority simply replaces the older decision: newest human decision wins, one Forget still revokes the only active record, 0118); if none exists a NEW row is inserted with the caller's id and `provenance` encoded with it (`status: 'inserted'`) — a REVOKED row is NEVER reactivated: it stays as history beside the new row (the partial index ignores revoked rows, so the insert succeeds). NEW `listHumanDecisions({ appId, agentFolder, actingPersonId, includeRevoked? })` ordered newest first by `created_at`, person-scoped (no cross-person rows, pinned); `includeRevoked` defaults to false (active rows only); `true` returns revoked rows too, each with its `revokedAt` (pinned); NEW `revokeById({ appId, agentFolder, actingPersonId, recordId, nowIso })` → `'applied' | 'already_revoked' | 'not_found'` — `not_found` when the id exists for ANOTHER person, app or agent folder (never crosses any of the three axes, pinned by cross-person, cross-app and cross-folder tests); NEW `countExactAllowsByTool({ appId, agentFolder, actingPersonId })` → `Record<toolName, number>` of ACTIVE `outcome = allow`, `scope = exact` rows grouped by the canonical tool name carried in `principal` (the human row stores AC3's `canonicalTool` in the existing `principal` column — the trust-growth input read by T5a; documented in the architecture note). `getClassifierVerdict`/`putClassifierVerdict` are byte-identical. Tests: Postgres round-trips for each new method per person; unit guard test for the refusals.
